items.title: ASA Pushes Back on Insurer Claims That the No Surprises Act IDR Process Is Broken
items.reason: The item directly addresses disputes over the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process implementation, which is a core component of the litigation and enforcement landscape the topic covers.
items.summary: The American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) has responded to insurance industry claims that the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process is dysfunctional. The ASA's pushback addresses insurer arguments about how the IDR mechanism is operating, which is relevant to revenue-cycle teams because disputes over IDR process efficacy directly affect how out-of-network billing disputes are resolved and payment determinations are made under the No Surprises Act framework.

items.title: UnitedHealthcare Long-Term Disability Denials & Appeals (2026) - sokolovelaw.com
items.reason: This item reports on UnitedHealthcare claims-denial practices involving long-term disability benefits, which falls directly under payer litigation and enforcement involving claims-denial issues and regulatory scrutiny of a major national health insurer.
items.summary: UnitedHealthcare is facing scrutiny regarding its long-term disability claims-denial and appeals processes as of 2026. The matter involves allegations of improper denials and inadequate appeals procedures for disabled claimants seeking long-term disability benefits through UnitedHealthcare. This development is relevant to revenue-cycle teams as it reflects ongoing regulatory and legal pressure on major payers' claims-handling practices, which can influence broader payer compliance standards and claims processing requirements that affect provider reimbursement and payment cycles.
